# [pytorch compile] Incorrect result when `dtype` changes

<!-- DRAFT generated by tcc. Review every section before filing (plan 18.6). -->

## Summary
The compiled execution is inconsistent with Python eager execution when `dtype` changes from `float16` to `(base)`.
divergence already present at backend='eager': Dynamo graph-capture semantics (often documented-unsupported behaviour)
This test was generated because the static analysis found: numerics depend on precision regardless of source (factor `x.dtype`, oracles ['value', 'metadata']).

## Environment
- Python: 3.12.13
- Framework: PyTorch 2.10.0+cu128
- Compiler backend: inductor
- Commit/version: 449b1768410104d3ed79d3bcfe4ba1d65c7f22c0
- CUDA/ROCm: 12.8
- GPU: Tesla T4
- OS: Linux 6.12.90+
- Triton: 3.6.0

## Minimal Reproducer

```python
import torch
torch.manual_seed(0)

def loss(x):
    return SinWithZeroBackward.apply(x).sum()

args = (torch.randn(4).to(torch.float16),)

eager = loss(*args)
torch._dynamo.reset()
compiled = torch.compile(loss, backend='eager')(*args)
print('eager   :', eager)
print('compiled:', compiled)
```

## Expected Behavior

Eager/reference result:

```text
structure: T
[0] [0, 0, 0, 0]
```

## Actual Behavior

Compiled result:

```text
exception InternalTorchDynamoError: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named '_repro_issue_193279_dynamo_silently_drops_custom_backward_of'
```

## Trigger Condition

Changed semantic factor:

```text
dtype: float16 -> (base)
```

Controlled factors:

```text
shape / dtype / stride / device / compile flags: unchanged
```

Execution sequence:

```text
E0_eager: ok
E1_dynamo_eager: InternalTorchDynamoError
E2_aot_eager: InternalTorchDynamoError
E3_inductor: InternalTorchDynamoError
```

## Accuracy methodology

A float64 reference was computed; numeric findings are reported only when the compiled error against that reference exceeds the eager error by more than the configured multiplier.

## Possible existing issues

- https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/193279 — origin issue of this reproducer
- https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/192985 — Dynamo silently drops custom `jvp` of `autograd.Function` under `torch.func.jvp`, producing wrong tangents
- https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/193277 — Fix Dynamo silently dropping custom jvp of autograd.Function under forward AD
